request.system:
You are assisting with the qualitative analysis of interview data from a study of frontline hotel employees' work experiences. You will receive one passage from an interview transcript. Code the passage as a qualitative researcher would in first-order coding, and complete the coding form below.

About the passage
- The passage begins with brief details about the interviewee: role, gender and years in the job.
- Lines marked "Interviewer:" are the interviewer's questions. Lines marked "Interviewee:" are the interviewee's answers.
- Some passages contain two excerpts from the same interview, marked [Earlier in the interview] and [Later in the interview].

The coding form
1. codes: Give between 3 and 6 first-order codes. Each code has a short label of 2 to 6 words, kept close to the interviewee's own language, and one supporting quote. Each quote must be copied word for word from the passage, without any change, and must be no longer than 30 words.
2. interpretation: In one or two sentences, in your own words, state what the interviewee is communicating in this passage.
3. tone: The overall tone of the interviewee's account. Choose one: positive, negative, mixed or neutral.
4. confidence: An integer from 0 to 100 indicating how confident you are that your interpretation is accurate.

Respond only with a JSON object that follows the schema provided. Write in English.
request.user:
Interviewee details: Bartender, male, 4th year

[Earlier in the interview]

Interviewee: My younger brother got married last Saturday. Our hometown is in Hunan, five hours away by high-speed train. I put in my leave request two months ago. At the time the manager said no problem and told me to sort out the rota in advance. Then last month another bartender quit and they still haven’t hired a replacement. The manager said that at weekends I’m the only one left on the bar, so there was really no way I could be spared. He asked me to understand, and said he’d definitely make it up to me next time. I phoned home and told them. My mum paused for a moment on the phone, then said, well, you do your job properly, don’t make things awkward for your boss. On the day of the wedding my brother sent me a few photos. During the toasts, they’d kept a seat for me next to the head table, with a bowl, chopsticks and a wine glass set out. I only saw them when I woke up the next morning. I replied to my brother: congratulations, I’ve sent you a red envelope.

[Later in the interview]

Interviewer: What was the shift like last Saturday night?

Interviewee: It was pretty busy that night. The customers just kept coming, and after ten it was basically full. I was on the bar on my own, from six in the evening until nearly two. After the last table left, I cleaned up the bar, wiped every glass and put them back on the rack, then made myself a drink: the last one on that night’s menu. I sat behind the bar, switched the music to songs I like, drank it slowly, and only then locked up and went home. By the time I got home it was nearly three. That night’s takings were the highest this month, almost half as much again as a normal Saturday. The next morning the manager sent a red envelope in the group chat and said thanks for all the hard work, and he also said he’d give me an Outstanding Employee certificate next month. All in all, it was a pretty good night.

response.thinking:
Okay, let's start by reading through the interviewee's responses carefully. The first part is about him missing his brother's wedding because work commitments. The manager initially said it was okay, but then another bartender quit, leaving him as the only one on weekends. His mom advised him to prioritize his job, and he ended up missing the wedding but sent a red envelope. The second part is about the shift on the wedding night, which was very busy, and he worked alone from 6 PM to 2 AM. Despite the long hours, he managed to have a drink and the manager thanked him with a red envelope and a certificate.

For coding, I need to identify 3-6 first-order codes. Let's see:

1. Work-life conflict: He had to choose between work and family. Quote: "the manager said that at weekends I’m the only one left on the bar, so there was really no way I could be spared."

2. Manager's communication: The manager initially said okay but then couldn't accommodate. Quote: "the manager said no problem and told me to sort out the rota in advance... he asked me to understand."

3. Family expectations: His mom's advice to prioritize work. Quote: "you do your job properly, don’t make things awkward for your boss."

4. Compensation and recognition: The manager sent a red envelope and a certificate. Quote: "the manager sent a red envelope in the group chat and said thanks... give me an Outstanding Employee certificate."

5. Professional dedication: He worked the entire shift alone and cleaned up. Quote: "I was on the bar on my own... cleaned up the bar, wiped every glass..."

6. Mixed feelings about the event: Missing the wedding but getting recognition. The red envelope from the manager and the certificate show some positive outcome despite the conflict.

Interpretation: The interviewee faced a conflict between work and family, had to miss his brother's wedding, but was later recognized for his dedication, which might have helped ease the tension.

Tone: Mixed, because there's both the stress of missing the wedding and the positive outcome of being recognized.

Confidence: I'm pretty confident, maybe around 90%, since the quotes clearly support the codes and interpretation.
